talks.title: Sylvester Tremmel - [EN] APT Down and the mystery of the burning data centers
talks.teaser: Presenters detail vulnerability discovery and exploitation in Sylvester Tremmel - [EN] APT Down and the mystery of the burning data centers.
talks.summary:
Journalists on the APT Down Dump

Sylvester Tremmel and colleague Christopher Kunz summarize c't reporting on a leaked workstation belonging to threat actor Kim, likely linked to North Korea's Kimsuky APT, while urging researchers to explore the dump themselves.

What the Dump Contains

Researchers shoulder-surfed Kim using Deepin Linux VMs, capturing messy desktops with Cobalt Strike beacons, Ivanti webshells, rootkits, phishing results against South Korean targets, and a previously unknown Linux rootkit.

Attribution Clues

Kim may be a Chinese national working North Korean hours, using Chinese fonts and struggling with Korean OCR. Tremmel stresses Kim is a cybercriminal, not a hobby hacker.

Burning Data Centers Mystery

The talk title references follow-on reporting about destructive attacks on data centers tied to the broader APT Down investigation, with Korean translation and document-format challenges complicating analysis.
